task_instruction: Plan a mystery-themed reading week for third graders linking to local history
task_details: Third grade cross-curricular week combining mystery picture books with local history. Goal is to build inference skills and civic awareness over five library visits in a two-week span. Library to provide read-alouds, three picture book titles, detective notebooks for students, and a short culminating class presentation. Teacher to align morning meeting prompts and one social studies mini-lesson. Schedule visit dates and share responsibilities; order two extra copies if possible.
personalized:
Hi Ana,

¿qué tal? I'd love to team up on a mystery-themed reading week that ties into our local history unit for third grade. My idea: five short library visits across two weeks where we build inference skills with picture-book mysteries and a focus on community places. I can bring three picture books (I was thinking a gentle town mystery, a historical mystery picture book, and a bilingual title), create detective notebooks for each student, and run the read-alouds and a short inference mini-lesson (I can cover circulation that week). Would you be open to doing a morning-meeting prompt on clue-gathering each day and teaching a 10-minute social studies connection to the place featured in the story?

Logistics we should confirm: visit dates that work for your class, I can order two extra copies if we want small-group reads (budget permitting), and I'll prepare a one-page family note so students can share the project at home. What do you think about starting the week of the 15th? I can draft the schedule and drop it in your mailbox (or email it), and I already have a stack of detective notebooks we can personalize.

Looking forward to scheming — in the friendliest, most librarian way possible. Would you like me to bring a scarf and a magnifying glass for dramatic effect? (I knit while I read, so expect calm energy.)

Abrazos, María

  - Optional: bring a scarf and a magnifying glass as props for dramatic effect

  - Lead a morning-meeting prompt on clue-gathering each day of the visits
  - Teach a 10-minute social studies connection to the place featured in each story

Dear Superintendent,

I am writing to report outcomes from a pilot of cross-curricular literacy units integrating ELA and Social Studies at two elementary schools. The pilot included four units reaching approximately 320 students. Teacher feedback was positive, noting increased student engagement with historical texts and higher-quality text-dependent discussions. Assessment data show an average 12 percent gain in reading comprehension on unit-aligned measures.

The pilot was budget neutral, leveraging existing texts and teacher planning time. Lessons learned include the need for pacing guides and additional anchor texts for small-group differentiation. Based on outcomes, I recommend district adoption with minor adjustments to support teachers and align to pacing calendars.

May we schedule a meeting to discuss scaling and curriculum alignment? Thank you for reviewing this promising instructional approach.

Sincerely,
María López, M.S., Library and Information Science

Best regards

Dear Front-Desk/Circulation Staff,

As part of our ongoing efforts to ensure a seamless and efficient library experience, we are introducing a standardized lost-item recovery procedure. This new process aims to provide consistency and fairness in handling lost-item recoveries. Please take a moment to review the following key policy details and required staff actions:

- Items more than 30 days overdue will be billed at replacement cost plus a processing fee, unless the patron chooses to replace the exact item themselves.

I'll be bringing extra patience to our reading time next Thursday to make sure everything runs smoothly.

Best regards,
María

As we work to maintain healthy stacks, it's essential to follow the donation intake process carefully. Please direct donors to bring their donations to the counter, where they will be processed accordingly.

María

task_instruction: Submit a letter of intent to apply for a larger multi-year literacy grant.
task_details: Send a concise letter of intent indicating intention to apply for a $75,000, three-year literacy expansion grant to scale 'Neighborhood Readers' partnership across two more elementary schools, reaching 800 students. personalized:
Dear Grant Officer,

This letter serves as our formal intent to apply for the multi-year literacy expansion grant for $75,000 over three years. Our proposal will expand the 'Neighborhood Readers' model to two additional elementary schools, reaching an estimated 800 students with bundled reading interventions, family literacy nights, and professional development for staff.

Anticipated outcomes include a district-wide increase in library circulation among K–3 students, measurable reading gains as shown on benchmark assessments, and a documented model for replication with our county library partner. Key partners include Sacramento County Library and neighboring school districts; we plan to submit the full proposal by March 1, 2026.

Thank you for the opportunity to indicate intent. I will follow with the formal application and materials. Please contact me at marialopez@lincolnlib.org or (916) 555-0123 for any preliminary questions.

Sincerely,

María López
Elementary School Librarian
